$$

$$
\begin{aligned}2 x -3 y=-5 \\ -3 y &= -2 x -5 \\ y &= \frac{2 x}{3} + \frac{5}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Since perpendicular lines have slopes that are negative reciprocals of each other, the slope of the new line should be the negative reciprocal of the slope of the given line. The given line has a slope of $\frac{2}{3},$ so our perpendicular line must have a slope of $-\frac{3}{2}.$

Our perpendicular line must have the slope $m=-\frac{3}{2}$ and pass through the point $(x_1,y_1)=(-1,-4).$ Using point-slope form and simplifying, we obtain the equation of the line in slope-intercept form:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-y_1 &= m(x-x_1) \\ y-(-4) &= -\frac{3}{2}(x-(-1)) \\ y-(-4) &= -\frac{3 x}{2} -\frac{3}{2} \\ y &= -\frac{3 x}{2} -\frac{11}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

However, we want to write the equation in standard form. So, we will bring the $x$ term to the left-hand side and multiply both sides of the equation by $2:$

$$
\begin{aligned}y &= -\frac{3 x}{2} -\frac{11}{2} \\ \frac{3 x}{2} + y &= -\frac{11}{2} \\ 2(\frac{3 x}{2} + y) &= 2(-\frac{11}{2}) \\ 3 x + 2 y &= -11\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}y-y_1 &= m(x-x_1) \\ y-(4) &= -1(x-(-3)) \\ y-(4) &= -x -3 \\ y &= 1 -x\end{aligned}
$$
